examples.japanese: {秤|はかり}で{野菜|やさい}の{重|おも}さを{量|はか}る。
examples.english: Weigh the vegetables on the scales.

examples.japanese: キッチン{秤|はかり}で{小麦粉|こむぎこ}を200グラム{量|はか}った。
examples.english: I measured 200 grams of flour on the kitchen scale.

examples.japanese: {体重計|たいじゅうけい}に{乗|の}るのが{怖|こわ}い。
examples.english: I'm afraid to step on the bathroom scale.
examples.notes: [Note: {体重計|たいじゅうけい} is specifically a body weight scale]

notes:
{秤|はかり} is the general term for a weighing device — any type of scale or balance. Also sometimes written as はかり in hiragana or {計|はかり}.

TYPES OF SCALES:
- キッチン{秤|はかり}: kitchen scale
- デジタル{秤|はかり}: digital scale
- {台秤|だいばかり}: platform scale
- {天秤|てんびん}: balance scale (also figurative: weighing options)
- {体重計|たいじゅうけい}: bathroom/body weight scale (uses {計|けい} not {秤|はかり})

RELATED VOCABULARY:
- {量|はか}る / {計|はか}る: to measure, to weigh
- {重|おも}さ: weight
- {計量|けいりょう}: measurement

NOTE:
The kanji {秤|はかり} is not a common-use kanji ({常用漢字|じょうようかんじ}), so it is often written in hiragana. In stores, {量|はか}り{売|う}り means "sold by weight."
